question: A 28-year-old man is admitted after consuming pesticide. The family insists it was accidental and requests that no police documentation be done to avoid stigma. As the treating doctor, which is the CORRECT legal approach in India?

answers.text: Respect the family's wishes; document as accidental since the family confirms it

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The family's assertion of 'accidental' does not exempt the case from MLC registration. Only the courts determine intent — the doctor's duty is documentation, not judgement of intent.

answers.text: Register the case as a medico-legal case (MLC) and inform the police regardless of the family's wishes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Every poisoning case in India is, by law, a medico-legal case. The treating doctor MUST register an MLC and inform the police. This is a non-negotiable legal duty under Indian law. Failure to do so constitutes professional misconduct. The family's wishes cannot override this statutory obligation.

answers.text: Wait for psychiatric assessment to confirm deliberate self-harm before registering the MLC

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MLC registration does not require confirmation of suicidal intent. Any poisoning — accidental, deliberate, or suspected — must be registered as MLC. Psychiatric assessment happens in addition to MLC registration, not as a prerequisite.

answers.text: Register as MLC only if the patient dies or becomes critically ill

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MLC registration is mandatory for ALL poisoning cases, not only fatal or critical ones. Severity does not determine MLC status — the nature of the injury (poisoning) does.

overallFeedback.feedback: In India, all poisoning cases are medico-legal cases (MLC) by definition — regardless of presumed intent, severity, or family preference. The doctor must register and inform police. This is a legal duty, not a clinical judgement.
Correct. Every poisoning in India is an MLC. The treating doctor has a non-negotiable legal duty to register it and inform police. Family preference cannot override this statutory obligation.
